List a pair's price-limit pools on a chain, deepest first, with their prices.

Usage: sauce pools --chain <slug|id> <token> <token> [--v4-key <fee:spacing>]… [--block <number|tag>] [--json]
       sauce pools --chain solana <pay token> <buy token> [--json]

Options:
      --chain <slug|id>  The chain the pools are on
      --rpc-url <url>    Your own RPC endpoint for the chain (default: a built-in public one)
      --config <file>    Or a file of your own: { "rpcUrls": { "<chain id>": "<url>" } }
      --offline          Read no chain: no endpoint, not even a built-in one
      --json             Print one JSON object instead
  -h, --help             Show this help

EVM chains only:
      --v4-key <fee:spacing>  Also try this hookless Uniswap V4 pool key (3000:60)
      --block <number|tag>    Read the pools at this block: a number, or latest, safe, finalized (default: latest)

Every pool of the pair at the price-limit venues the registry records on the chain:
Uniswap V3 and PancakeSwap V3 at each fee tier their factory enables, Aerodrome Slipstream
at each tick spacing of each of its CLFactories, and hookless Uniswap V4 pools at the keys
100:1, 500:10, 3000:60 and 10000:200, and any --v4-key. A token is a symbol the chain
registers (sauce globals --tokens), or an address: its decimals and symbol are read from
the token (or give them, 0x…:8).

Pools with liquidity come first, deepest first: by the liquidity at each pool's price,
which is in the same units at every venue for one pair. For each: the venue and the
contract a program finds it through, its address (a V4 pool's id and key), its fee read
from the pool (a V4 pool's LP fee and protocol fee, from StateView), tick spacing,
liquidity, tick and sqrtPriceX96, and both ways round: what one token costs in the other
before and with the fee, the distributed swap's maxPrice at that price (pay base units per
buy base unit times 1e18: the price times 10^(18 + pay decimals - buy decimals)), and about
how much of the paid token, fee included, moves the price 1% against the taker, walked
through the pool's ticks. Pools with no liquidity at their price are listed after them, as
skipped. Then what was looked at.

It reads the chain in five requests, each one eth_call for every read in it, all at one
block, which it names: --block, or the latest when it starts. Pass that block to sauce
simulate --block to rehearse on the prices maxPrice was taken from.

On Solana: every pool of the pair at each venue whose swap takes a price limit that stops

8	// The accounts, by name, in one JSON object (or each as --account NAME=<value>):
9	//   authority     pot: the Pot, which signs for its accounts (owner, cooked with --via engine)
10	//   source        pot:<payToken>: the authority's account the budget is in
11	//   output        pot:<buyToken>: the authority's account what is bought arrives in
12	//   recipient     the account what is bought goes on to (output itself, to keep it there)
13	//   refund        the account what is left of the budget goes to (source itself, to keep it)
14	//   payMint       mint:<payToken>; buyMint, mint:<buyToken>

Rehearse the cook from the Pot's owner, with no key: what it did, or why it reverts.
Usage: sauce simulate <file | -> --chain <slug|id> (--owner <address> | --pot <address>) [options]
       sauce simulate <file | -> --chain solana --owner <pubkey> [--account NAME=<value>]… [options]
      --owner <address>                            The Pot's owner, which derives the Pot with the salt (default 0)
      --salt <label>                               Name one of the owner's Pots: salt = keccak256(label)
      --config <file>                              Or a file of your own: { "rpcUrls": { "<chain id>": "<url>" } }
      --assume-balance <TOKEN:amount>              Give the Pot this balance, in whole tokens, for the rehearsal only: USDC:2, ETH:0.1
      --wallet <name>                              The owner's wallet: names the owner (and on EVM signs --fund's pulls)
      --keystore <path>      The owner's keystore: names the owner (and signs --fund's pulls)
      --account NAME=<address>        An account main takes, by name: an address, pot, owner, pot:USDC (the Pot's USDC account), mint:USDC or program:USDC (its token program)
      --accounts <json|file>          The accounts main takes as one JSON object of NAME to value, as --account takes them, inline or in a file
      --lookup-table <address>        An address lookup table holding the cook's accounts (sauce run creates one when they do not fit)
      --keypair <path>                The owner's keypair, naming the owner; nothing is signed
Compiles the file, builds the cook and rehearses it from the Pot's owner: no key, no
A Pot that is not deployed yet is deployed in the rehearsal first, from --owner (and
--salt): any account may send Kitchen.deployPot, and the Pot is the owner's either way.
An owner holding less than the cook's value is given it for the rehearsal.
--assume-balance TOKEN:amount gives the Pot that balance for this rehearsal only, by state
With --fund and the owner's key (--keystore or --private-key), the rehearsal includes the
On Solana: the Kitchen cook, simulated from --owner with signatures unchecked, with each
account main takes given as --account NAME=<address | pot | owner> and an Address
for that mint, its associated token account under the mint's token program; owner:USDC the
owner's; mint:USDC the mint and program:USDC its token program (SPL Token or Token-2022),
the accounts a checked write takes. An account the cluster does not have is named in a
no Pot (so no pot or pot:<token> account), --owner signing as the program's authority and
accounts the transaction writes before it and as the simulation leaves them — or the reason
takes no account overrides, so the owner must hold the Pot's rent and the fees there.
A cook too large for one transaction, or one given --assume-balance, is rehearsed in a
local copy instead (LiteSVM, which the project must have: npm install litesvm): every
its accounts through a lookup table. There --assume-balance TOKEN:amount gives the account
the cook spends that token from (the Pot's, or the owner's with --via engine) that balance,
and a pot:<token> or owner:<token> account the cluster does not have yet is made empty,
  sauce simulate pay.sauce.ts --chain base --owner 0x… \
    --assume-balance USDC:2 --args 0x… 1000000
  sauce simulate sweep.sauce.ts --chain solana --owner <pubkey> \
  sauce simulate sweep.sauce.ts --chain solana --owner <pubkey> \
    --via engine --account source=<token account> --account authority=owner

I wrote and rehearsed the swap with no key and sent nothing, but **`sauce simulate` never reported a successful cook.** Every rehearsal ended with `InsufficientFundsForRent`, even a one-line program that only returns `x + 1`. The program logs show the swap itself did run and succeed inside that rehearsal.

**The trade:** sell 500 USDC for SOL, never below 0.0084 SOL per USDC, which is at most 119.047619 USDC per SOL.
- `budget` = `500000000`
- `maxPrice` = `119047619047619047`
- `minTokens` = `4200000001`: all 500 USDC at the floor or nothing.
- `maxAvgPrice` = `118370887860913802`: halfway between the rehearsed average and `maxPrice`.

**The venues:** I used USDC/WSOL with one slot per venue that has a pool within the limit, deepest first:

| Slot | Venue | Fee | Pool |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Orca Whirlpools | 0.04% | `Czfq…44zE` |
| 1 | Raydium CLMM | 0.04% | `3ucN…uxv` |
| 2 | PancakeSwap CLMM | 0.01% | `DJNt…6rsZ` |
| 3 | DefiTuna | 0.05% | `7VuK…t65` |
| 4 | Cropper | 0.02% | `55Tu…doQ` |

The other price-limit venues are left out for these reasons:
- **Crema, Stabble and Phoenix:** their best prices are past the limit (about 121, 122 and 129 USDC per SOL).
- **Byreal:** its only pool has more than one fee rate.

The skill's program has four slots, so I added a fifth. The skill says about five pools fit in one transaction.

**What the rehearsal showed, from the engine's return data:**
- **Fill:** 500 USDC spent, 4.248299271 SOL bought, nothing unspent, for an average of about 117.69 USDC per SOL (0.008497 SOL per USDC, above your floor). Orca's pool was deep enough to take the whole order, so the other four slots had nothing left to trade, which is the intended behaviour.
- **Guards:** with `minTokens` set above the fill, and with `maxAvgPrice` set below the average, the engine reverted as it should.
- **Final arguments:** the engine completed the swap using about 400k of the 1.4M compute units.

**Why it doesn't report success:** the fee goes to the Kitchen's fee config, `DRBtuXHdgM2qjkC6rfZn6s1cMeU6rxauV5K9TVX5DpFs`. On the real cluster that account works: a small test program rehearsed there succeeds and pays it. The local copy doesn't seem to load its balance, so the 85,672-lamport fee leaves it below the rent minimum and the copy rejects the transaction. That points to a bug in the package's `sauce simulate` and needs fixing in `../sauce-sdk`. I couldn't read that source because access was blocked. Until it's fixed, the revert messages aren't shown either: the guard failures came back as the same rent error.

**Files and changes:**
- `sauce/sell-usdc-for-sol.sauce.ts`: the five-slot program.
- `sauce/sell-usdc-for-sol.accounts.json`: the accounts, using the Pot's own USDC and WSOL accounts.
- `litesvm` added to `devDependencies`, which local rehearsals need.

The throwaway owner `3jBT…MuU` was a random address used only for the rehearsal. Before a real `sauce run`, the Pot's USDC and WSOL accounts would need creating and funding. The pool prices were read at about Solana slot 454189460 and will drift.
